name: Manage Windows default User Rights
description: Legt de Windows-gebruikersrechten vast volgens CIS Level 1 en vervangt de User Rights uit de Windows 365-securitybaseline. Het gastaccount kan zich op geen enkele manier aanmelden, lokale accounts (zoals LAPS) kunnen niet via netwerk of RDP aanmelden, Backup Operators is verwijderd uit back-up, herstel en afsluiten, en ook de servicerechten zijn vastgelegd. Gevoelige systeemrechten liggen alleen bij Administrators. De Print Spooler-service (Windows 11 24H2+) is opgenomen zodat afdrukken blijft werken. Alle rechten zijn op SID ingesteld en daardoor taalonafhankelijk. Geldt voor pc's en Cloud PC's.

settings.name: Access this computer from the network
settings.description: Determines which users and groups can connect to the device over the network, for example via SMB or RPC.
settings.rationale: Limiting network access to Administrators and Remote Desktop Users reduces the attack surface for lateral movement and credential misuse.

mappings.control: 2.2.2 (L1) Access this computer from the network: Administrators, Remote Desktop Users

settings.name: Adjust memory quotas for a process
settings.description: Determines who can change the maximum amount of memory a process can consume.
settings.rationale: Misuse of this right can be used for denial-of-service attacks; restricting it to Administrators and built-in service accounts prevents abuse.

mappings.control: 2.2.4 (L1) Adjust memory quotas for a process: Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE

settings.name: Allow log on locally
settings.description: Determines which users can sign in interactively at the device.
settings.rationale: Only legitimate users and administrators should be able to sign in locally; Guests and Backup Operators are excluded.

mappings.control: 2.2.5 (L1) Allow log on locally: Administrators, Users

settings.name: Back up files and directories
settings.description: Allows bypassing file and directory permissions to back up the system.
settings.rationale: This right allows reading any file regardless of ACLs. Restricting it to Administrators (Backup Operators removed) prevents data exfiltration.

mappings.control: 2.2.7 (L1) Back up files and directories: Administrators

settings.name: Create global objects
settings.value: Administrators (*S-1-5-32-544), LOCAL SERVICE (*S-1-5-19), NETWORK SERVICE (*S-1-5-20), SERVICE (*S-1-5-6)
settings.description: Determines who can create global objects that are available to all sessions.
settings.rationale: Users with this right could create objects that affect processes in other sessions, which can lead to privilege escalation or data corruption.

mappings.control: 2.2.12 (L1) Create global objects: Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE

settings.name: Create a pagefile
settings.description: Determines who can create and change the size of the page file.
settings.rationale: Manipulating the page file can degrade system performance or expose memory contents; only Administrators need this right.

mappings.control: 2.2.10 (L1) Create a pagefile: Administrators

settings.name: Debug programs
settings.description: Determines who can attach a debugger to any process or the kernel.
settings.rationale: This right gives full access to process memory and is frequently abused for credential theft (e.g. LSASS dumping); restrict to Administrators.

mappings.control: 2.2.15 (L1) Debug programs: Administrators

settings.name: Deny access to this computer from the network
settings.description: Prevents the specified accounts from connecting to the device over the network.
settings.rationale: Blocking Guests and local accounts (including LAPS-managed accounts) from network logon prevents lateral movement with local credentials.

mappings.control: 2.2.16 (L1) Deny access to this computer from the network: Guests, Local account

settings.name: Deny log on locally
settings.description: Prevents the specified accounts from signing in interactively at the device.
settings.rationale: The Guest account should never be able to sign in to the device.

mappings.control: 2.2.19 (L1) Deny log on locally: Guests

settings.name: Deny log on as a batch job
settings.description: Prevents the specified accounts from signing in through a batch-queue facility such as Task Scheduler.
settings.rationale: Prevents the Guest account from being used to run scheduled tasks.

mappings.control: 2.2.17 (L1) Deny log on as a batch job: Guests

settings.name: Deny log on as a service
settings.description: Prevents the specified accounts from registering a process as a service.
settings.rationale: Prevents the Guest account from being used to run services.

mappings.control: 2.2.18 (L1) Deny log on as a service: Guests

settings.name: Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services
settings.description: Prevents the specified accounts from signing in through Remote Desktop.
settings.rationale: Blocking Guests and local accounts from RDP prevents remote access with local or LAPS credentials.

mappings.control: 2.2.20 (L1) Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services: Guests, Local account

settings.name: Generate security audits
settings.description: Determines which accounts can write entries to the Security event log.
settings.rationale: Attackers with this right could flood or forge security log entries. The Print Spooler virtual account (Windows 11 24H2+) is added so printing keeps working.

mappings.control: 2.2.23 (L1) Generate security audits: LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE

settings.name: Impersonate a client after authentication
settings.description: Allows programs running on behalf of a user to impersonate that client.
settings.rationale: Impersonation can be abused for privilege escalation (e.g. potato-style attacks). The Print Spooler virtual account (Windows 11 24H2+) is added so printing keeps working.

mappings.control: 2.2.24 (L1) Impersonate a client after authentication: Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE

settings.name: Increase scheduling priority
settings.description: Determines which accounts can raise the base priority class of a process.
settings.rationale: A user with this right could raise process priority to make the system unresponsive (denial of service).

mappings.control: 2.2.25 (L1) Increase scheduling priority: Administrators, Window Manager\Window Manager Group

settings.name: Load and unload device drivers
settings.description: Determines who can dynamically load and unload device drivers.
settings.rationale: Loading a malicious or vulnerable driver gives kernel-level access; only Administrators should hold this right.

mappings.control: 2.2.26 (L1) Load and unload device drivers: Administrators

settings.name: Manage auditing and security log
settings.description: Determines who can configure object access auditing and view or clear the Security log.
settings.rationale: Users with this right could clear the Security log to hide malicious activity.

mappings.control: 2.2.30 (L1) Manage auditing and security log: Administrators

settings.name: Perform volume maintenance tasks
settings.description: Determines who can run volume maintenance tasks such as defragmentation.
settings.rationale: This right allows raw access to volumes and could be used to read or delete data; restrict to Administrators.

mappings.control: 2.2.33 (L1) Perform volume maintenance tasks: Administrators

settings.name: Modify firmware environment values
settings.description: Determines who can modify firmware (UEFI/NVRAM) environment variables.
settings.rationale: Changing firmware values can compromise boot integrity or make the device unusable.

mappings.control: 2.2.32 (L1) Modify firmware environment values: Administrators

settings.name: Profile single process
settings.description: Determines who can use performance monitoring tools on non-system processes.
settings.rationale: Process profiling can reveal sensitive information about running applications.

mappings.control: 2.2.34 (L1) Profile single process: Administrators

settings.name: Profile system performance
settings.description: Determines who can use performance monitoring tools on system processes.
settings.rationale: System profiling can reveal sensitive information; only Administrators and the Diagnostic Service Host need this right.

mappings.control: 2.2.35 (L1) Profile system performance: Administrators, NT SERVICE\WdiServiceHost

settings.name: Force shutdown from a remote system
settings.description: Determines who can shut down the device from a remote location on the network.
settings.rationale: Unauthorized remote shutdown causes denial of service.

mappings.control: 2.2.22 (L1) Force shutdown from a remote system: Administrators

settings.name: Replace a process level token
settings.description: Determines which accounts can change the access token of a child process.
settings.rationale: Token replacement can be used to start processes with elevated privileges; only built-in service accounts need this right.

mappings.control: 2.2.36 (L1) Replace a process level token: LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE

settings.name: Restore files and directories
settings.description: Allows bypassing file and directory permissions when restoring files.
settings.rationale: This right allows overwriting any file, including system binaries. Restricting it to Administrators (Backup Operators removed) prevents tampering.

mappings.control: 2.2.37 (L1) Restore files and directories: Administrators

settings.name: Shut down the system
settings.description: Determines which locally signed-in users can shut down the device.
settings.rationale: Users need to be able to shut down their device; Backup Operators is removed as it does not need this right.

mappings.control: 2.2.38 (L1) Shut down the system: Administrators, Users

settings.name: Take ownership of files or other objects
settings.description: Determines who can take ownership of any securable object, such as files, registry keys and processes.
settings.rationale: Taking ownership bypasses all object permissions; only Administrators should hold this right.

mappings.control: 2.2.39 (L1) Take ownership of files or other objects: Administrators

changelog.notes: Release of Manage Windows default User Rights baseline version 1.0.0 (26 user rights, CIS Level 1, replaces Windows 365 security baseline User Rights)
